Ritu (CS): Nebula procurement asked for a one-page SLA summary for contracting. They want MUP definition, p95 latency target, credit calc + cap, and a short onboarding timeline. Renewal check in ~6 weeks. Can @Eli and @Sam confirm numbers?
Eli (SRE): Hosted MUP = 99.9% (we call it monthly uptime percentage). p95 target ~350ms on standard endpoints. Dedicated: 99.95% MUP; expect p95 inflation during the first 30-90m after deploy (warm-up).
Sam (Solutions): wording suggestion: "Latency SLOs measured on steady-state traffic; transient increases during model swaps, cache warm-ups, or initial rollouts are documented in onboarding guidance."
Ritu (CS): credits: procurement wants a simple formula + tiny example.
Eli (SRE): paste-friendly formula: `credit = round(min(0.3, max(0, (SLO_target - observed_MUP) / SLO_target)) * committed_monthly_fee, 2)` cap = 30%. Example: $10k/mo, target 99.9%, observed 99.6% -> credit ≈ $30.
Diego (AE): Nebula runs heavy nightly batches; recommend optional add-ons: reserved concurrency, 1hr pre-warm slot, and a 14-day onboarding healthcheck. Dedicated lead time 2-3 weeks.
Ritu (CS): action items: (1) Eli - paste final PromQL/dashboard link for MUP; (2) Sam - draft the one-pager + 1-row Hosted vs Dedicated table; (3) Diego - add pricing bullets for add-ons. I'll send to procurement Friday EOD.
ReminderBot: Reminder set to ping thread members 2024-08-01T09:00:00Z to finalize one-pager.
Eli (SRE): metric name confirmed: "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)". PromQL example to link: `sum_over_time(up{service="inference-api"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)`. Note: multi-region customers receive per-region SLOs; credits calculated per-region unless negotiated.
Sam (Solutions): I'll drop draft into https://redwood.docs/nebula/sla-draft by Thu 12:00 PT. Keep the onboarding timeline short: Day 0 kickoff, Day 1 keys + smoke, Day 3 canary + tune, Day 7 scale.
Ritu (CS): perfect, thanks team :thumbsup:
